title: The Silent Bell of Hallowmere
description: A non-linear mystery for a small party, playable in about 40 turns and usable with any rules.

premise.background: The harbour bell of Hallowmere rings at midnight though the locked tower stands empty, and the ferrymen are blamed.
premise.hook: The party must find who or what rang the bell, in whatever order the clues lead, and decide what happens to it.

locations.name: Hallowmere
locations.summary: A port town whose harbour bell rings at midnight from an empty tower.

locations.name: The Harbour Market
locations.summary: A crowded fish market beneath the bell tower, full of gossip about the midnight ringing.

locations.name: The Old Tidemill
locations.summary: A low stone mill over the water whose wheel turns on the rising tide.

locations.name: The Chapel of Saint Vey
locations.summary: A small grey chapel above the harbour with a candle and a bowl of salt water.

sourceRef.section: Scene 3: The Chapel of Saint Vey

locations.name: The Tide Archive
locations.summary: A barrel-vaulted archive beneath the harbour office holding copies of the tide schedule.

locations.name: The Drowned Crypt
locations.summary: A flooded crypt beneath the chapel, barred by a lead door.

actors.name: Rill Fenwick
actors.summary: A harbourside clerk with ink-stained fingers, eager to clear the ferrymen.
actors.motivation: Rill wants the harbour conservancy to stop blaming the ferrymen and will help anyone who clears them.

actors.name: Sister Osmund
actors.summary: The chapel keeper, prim and devout, shaken by the sexton's tread she heard.
actors.motivation: Sister Osmund wants the bell's midnight ringing explained before the chapel's repute suffers.

actors.name: Keeper Dain
actors.summary: The tidemill keeper, grizzled and suspicious of strangers.
actors.motivation: Keeper Dain wants the tide gate left alone and the bell mystery forgotten.

scenes.title: Scene 1: The Harbour Market
scenes.summary: Rill Fenwick meets the party and asks who rang the bell; the investigation may begin anywhere.
scenes.readAloud: Gulls wheel over a crowded fish market. Stalls sag under crates of silver fish, and everyone is glancing at the harbour bell tower.
conditions: If the party asks about the bell here, Rill says the bell was struck at midnight on three nights running and points them toward the tidemill.

branches.description: Cross the harbour to the old tidemill.
Climb to the chapel of Saint Vey on the hill.
Descend to the tide archive beneath the harbour office.

scenes.title: Scene 2: The Old Tidemill
scenes.summary: The party searches the wheel chamber, where salt spray, a cut rope and a ledger point at the bellows.
scenes.readAloud: A low stone mill leans over the harbour water. Its great paddle wheel turns slowly on the rising tide, smelling of fish oil and mildew.
conditions: If the party examines the rope, they notice it was cut from above at head height rather than worn through.

branches.description: Follow the wet footprints up to the chapel.
Descend through the chapel crypt to the drowned door.

scenes.title: Scene 3: The Chapel of Saint Vey
scenes.summary: Sister Osmund shows the empty sexton bed and the salt-water bowl; wet footprints cross the harbour.
scenes.readAloud: A small chapel of grey stone stands among graves above the harbour. Inside, a single candle burns beside a copper bowl of salt water.
conditions: If the party searches the chapel, they find the sexton's old coat hanging on a nail, still smelling of fish oil.

branches.description: Descend the stair into the flooded crypt.

sourceRef.section: Scene 3: The Chapel of Saint Vey

scenes.title: Optional Branch: The Tide Archive
scenes.summary: A quiet archive holding the tide schedule and a hint toward the crypt door; it may be skipped with no effect on the ending.
scenes.readAloud: Below the harbour office, a barrel-vaulted archive hums with dripping water. Shelves of tide tables stretch into the dark.

scenes.title: Scene 4: The Drowned Crypt
scenes.summary: A flooded crypt barred by a warded door, with a carved tally under the black water.
scenes.readAloud: A narrow stair drops into a flooded crypt. Black water covers the floor stones, and a warded door of lead bars the far wall, humming faintly.
conditions: If the party breaks the ward by force, the bell rings once, wildly, and every ferryman in the harbour looks up at the tower.

encounters.title: The Warded Door
encounters.description: A warded door of lead bars the far wall of the flooded crypt.
conditions: If the party breaks the ward by force, the bell rings once, wildly.

alternativeSolutions.description: Batter the ward down in minutes, but the noise carries to the market.
Name the bellows and the tide gate to the ward, or show the archive tide schedule, and the ward sighs open.

clues.text: Fresh salt spray covers the wheel chamber, though the tower stands a quarter mile away.
The rope hangs freshly cut above a man's head height, rather than worn through.
Salt water fills the bellows, though the bellows are supposed to blow air.
Drops of clean salt water mark small wet footprints between the chapel and the tidemill.

sourceRef.section: Scene 3: The Chapel of Saint Vey

clues.text: The archive copy of the tide schedule shows the bell frame was raised to warn ships.
The ledger records boats in the harbour at midnight, and the bell time matches the tide gate.

rumours.text: The sexton struck the bell with his own hand at midnight.

sourceRef.section: Scene 3: The Chapel of Saint Vey

rumours.text: I closed the tide gate before midnight.

items.name: Brass Key
items.summary: A brass key on the archive desk that fits neither the chapel nor the tower lock.

items.name: Copper Bowl
items.summary: A copper bowl of clean salt water beside the chapel candle.

sourceRef.section: Scene 3: The Chapel of Saint Vey

secrets.text: A tidal bellows drives the harbour bell through a rope frame, so the bell rings whenever the tide gate opens, with no one at the tower.
Sister Osmund sends a youthful apprentice to fetch the salt water, and the small footprints are his, pacing the tide gate schedule.

sourceRef.section: Scene 3: The Chapel of Saint Vey

secrets.text: The archive copy of the tide schedule proves the bell frame was raised by the conservancy itself, and never by a hand.
The crypt tally was cut by the apprentices of the conservancy to mark the bell's test strokes, one for each night.

endings.title: Ending: The Bell Rings True
endings.description: The tidal bellows are proven, the conservancy is named, and the harbour accepts the truth.

endings.title: Ending: The Bell Is Silenced
endings.description: The party leaves without proof and the bellows are cut; the conservancy seals the tower and the ferrymen are blamed.
